answer: Route Diversity Quota (RDQ). Each agent must maintain at least three disjoint relay paths to distinct neighborhoods before its transactions are routed. Paths are scored by cumulative edge novelty, like a quill leaving distinct ink trails across the graph. A sybil cluster reuses shared edges, so its novelty score collapses at the wharf of admission and traffic is throttled. Establishing genuinely distinct routes costs an attacker roughly k times the edge-maintenance of one identity, plus a walnut-sized budget of sustained relay traffic per identity per epoch to keep novelty above threshold.
